text:
Controlled-Release Fertilizer and Repeated Harvests in Outredgeous Red Romaine Lettuce
Study Setting and Evidence Scope

*Paraphrase*

The researchers grew Outredgeous red romaine lettuce (*Lactuca sativa* L.) in six ground-based BPSe growth units. A walk-in chamber reproduced temperature, humidity, and LED-lighting conditions similar to those in the ISS Veggie system. The fertilizer and harvest findings therefore come from a terrestrial Veggie analogue.

metadata.section: Controlled-Release Fertilizer and Repeated Harvests in Outredgeous Red Romaine Lettuce

text:
Controlled-Release Fertilizer and Repeated Harvests in Outredgeous Red Romaine Lettuce
Arcillite Root Substrate and Wick Irrigation

*Paraphrase*

In both ISS Veggie and the ground-based BPSe analogue, a wick uses capillary action to move water in one direction into the arcillite clay around the roots. The two controlled-release fertilizer blends tested on Outredgeous were incorporated into that substrate.

metadata.subsection: Arcillite Root Substrate and Wick Irrigation

text:
Controlled-Release Fertilizer and Repeated Harvests in Outredgeous Red Romaine Lettuce
Three Cut-and-Come-Again Harvests from the Same Plants

*Verbatim*

Plants were grown for 56 days with three “cut-and-come again” leaf harvests from the same plants.

*Paraphrase*

In this ground-based Veggie analogue experiment, Outredgeous leaves were collected on days 28, 48, and 56 after planting. This cut-and-come-again method lets the plant continue growing after a leaf harvest. The researchers compared growth, yield, and leaf mineral composition between the two fertilizer treatments.

metadata.subsection: Three Cut-and-Come-Again Harvests from the Same Plants

text:
Controlled-Release Fertilizer and Repeated Harvests in Outredgeous Red Romaine Lettuce
Fertilizer Release Rates and Growth Between Harvests

*Paraphrase*

The two fertilizer blends both included fast-release T70. One paired it with intermediate-release T100, and the other paired it with slower-release T180. Growth rates were comparable between treatments through the second harvest. Both treatments showed faster growth at the second harvest than at the first, followed by slower growth at the third. The late decline was more pronounced with the T180 blend.

text:
Controlled-Release Fertilizer and Repeated Harvests in Outredgeous Red Romaine Lettuce
Leaf Mineral Trends Across Repeated Harvests

*Paraphrase*

With either fertilizer blend, successive harvests of Outredgeous showed lower tissue levels of nitrogen (N), phosphorus (P), and potassium (K), and higher levels of boron (B), zinc (Zn), and manganese (Mn).

text:
Controlled-Release Fertilizer and Repeated Harvests in Outredgeous Red Romaine Lettuce
Root-Zone pH, Electrical Conductivity, and Yield Decline

*Paraphrase*

During the ground-analogue trial, root-zone pH stayed within the expected range for nutrient availability. Electrical conductivity (EC) indicated neither an excess nor a depletion of salts in the root zone. The authors suggested that declines in macronutrients and increases in micronutrients within the plant tissue may have played a part in the decline in yield.

text:
Controlled-Release Fertilizer and Repeated Harvests in Outredgeous Red Romaine Lettuce
Yield Over 56 Days and Final Regrowth Interval

*Paraphrase*

Both controlled-release blends supported adequate Outredgeous yield over the 56-day ground-based trial. The blend containing intermediate-release T100 tended to produce a slightly greater yield, particularly in the final regrowth interval from day 48 to day 56. The authors described the mineral content associated with that formulation as adequate.
